title: META’s Zuckerberg, Wang Push Back On Calls To Slow AI Progress: ‘Alignment’ Could Set Leaders Apart
key_facts: Mark Zuckerberg, Meta chief executive, and Alexandr Wang, Meta's AI chief, posted on X on the pace of AI development.
They argued labs should continue advancing while building stronger safeguards.
Zuckerberg: 'Any lab that doesn't focus on alignment will fall behind.'
Both called for greater use of independent evaluators and external oversight.
Meta delayed the release of its Muse model for several months for safety and security work.
Wang called racing toward recursive self-improvement 'one of the riskiest pathways for potential loss of control to powerful models'.
quote_evidence: "People won't want to use agents that are misaligned with them and that don't do what they ask," Zuckerberg wrote.

"Committing the significant majority of compute towards serving people rather than racing towards recursive self-improvement is one of the best ways to ensure we develop this technology safely," Zuckerberg said.
why_it_matters_hint: Meta's leaders argue safety and outside review can coexist with continued fast AI development.
notes: Reply-type story: posts answer 'calls to slow AI' without naming a person; context names Amodei as the main voice for slowing. Posting date not stated (article published 14 Oct).
